title: Intersection and local detection calculus for subterminal module slices
statement:
Let $(\mathcal E,J)$ be a small subcanonical site with finite limits, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects such that $\{U,V\}\to1$ covers; put $W=U\times V$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Write $j_Z^*$ for restriction to $\mathcal E/Z$, and $k_U^*,k_V^*$ for restriction from $\mathcal E/U,\mathcal E/V$ to $\mathcal E/W$. For $Z=U,V,W$, the functor $j_Z^*$ has an additive exact left adjoint $j_{Z!}$, and both $j_Z^*$ and $j_{Z!}$ are exact. Explicitly $j_{Z!}F=P_F^\#$, where $P_F(C)=F(C\to Z)$ if there is a morphism $C\to Z$, and $P_F(C)=0$ otherwise, with scalar action induced by $R(C)$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The same notation $k_{U!},k_{V!}$ denotes extension within a slice. There are natural module-linear identifications
$$j_U^*j_{U!}\cong1,\quad j_U^*j_{V!}\cong k_{U!}k_V^*,\qquad j_V^*j_{V!}\cong1,\quad j_V^*j_{U!}\cong k_{V!}k_U^*.$$
These identifications commute with units, counits, and the nested-open maps defined by adjunction; restriction commutes with the sheafification in the displayed presheaf formulas. The pair $(j_U^*,j_V^*)$ jointly detects zero module sheaves and exactness of module sequences. On complexes and ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact restriction commutes with every $H^q$, jointly detects cohomological vanishing and quasi-isomorphisms, and restriction and extension by zero act termwise as triangulated functors.

source.place: Tags 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact) and 0F6Z (lemma-restrict-back); intersection exchange and joint zero/exactness tests for a covering pair of subterminals are the agent specialization and extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] with coefficient sheaf $R$ and object $Z$, for $Z=U,V,W$. It gives exact restriction and its exact left adjoint, constructed as the module sheafification of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Since $Z\hookrightarrow1$ is monic, any two arrows $C\to Z$ coincide. Thus the direct sum defining that presheaf has one summand $F(C\to Z)$ or no summands, giving exactly $P_F$ in the statement, with its specified $R(C)$-action and restrictions. Restriction is additive sectionwise; extension is additive because both the summand maps and sheafification preserve addition of morphisms (the latter follows from its linear universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]). Apply the same exact-adjunction lemma on $\mathcal E/U$ at $W\to U$ and on $\mathcal E/V$ at $W\to V$ to obtain $k_{U!}$ and $k_{V!}$. Their coefficient rings are the literal restrictions of $R$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); specialization to subterminal objects

proof.text: For $q:\mathcal E/Z\to\mathcal E$, every covering of $(C\to Z)$ is an underlying covering of $C$, and every covering of $C$ lifts to one of $(C\to Z)$ by composing its arrows with $C\to Z$. Pullbacks of these covering arrows are the same in the slice and the base. Thus $q$ is continuous and cocontinuous. The identical verification applies to further slice restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction] to these functors: restriction of $P^\#$ is canonically the sheafification of the restricted module presheaf, and the comparison sends the unit image of each presheaf section to the same unit image. This also fixes the normalization of all comparisons below. The smallness hypothesis holds for the slices, and their ring sheaves are restrictions along the identity coefficient map.

On an object $(C\to U)$, the presheaf extending $F$ from $\mathcal E/U$ evaluates to $F(C\to U)$, since the arrow to $U$ is unique. Consequently its restriction to $\mathcal E/U$ is exactly the already sheaf-valued presheaf $F$. Step 2 and the universal property of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] identify $j_U^*j_{U!}F$ with $F$, with the unit $F\to j_U^*j_{U!}F$ corresponding to the identity. Interchanging $U$ and $V$ gives the other self-restriction identification.

source.place: Tag 0F6Z (lemma-restrict-back), module-linear proof using the singleton-summand formula

proof.text: Let $F$ be an $R|_V$-module sheaf. At $(C,a:C\to U)$ the presheaf underlying $j_U^*j_{V!}F$ before sheafification is $F(C\to V)$ if $C\to V$ exists, and zero otherwise. An arrow $b:C\to V$ is equivalent, by the product universal property, to an arrow $(a,b):C\to W$ over $U$. The presheaf extending $k_V^*F$ from $\mathcal E/W$ to $\mathcal E/U$ therefore has precisely the same values. Its restrictions are those of $F$ when the source has an arrow to $V$, and zero out of a zero summand otherwise, on both sides. The scalar ring on each summand is $R(C)$ on both sides. Sheafifying this identity and using Step 2 gives $j_U^*j_{V!}\cong k_{U!}k_V^*$. The identity commutes with maps $F\to F'$, so is natural. Interchanging $U,V$ proves the remaining intersection identification.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 0F6Z; agent intersection calculation from the explicit presheaf

proof.text: The adjunction of Step 1 can be computed directly from the universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. A map $a:F\to j_Z^*G$ induces $j_{Z!}F\to G$ by sending a summand section $s\in F(C\to Z)$ to $a_{(C\to Z)}(s)\in G(C)$; conversely precompose a restricted map with the summand inclusion $F(C\to Z)\to P_F(C)\to P_F^\#(C)$. These operations are inverse, since every map out of the sheafification is determined on those summand sections. Hence the unit is this summand inclusion and the counit sends each summand section of $G(C)$ to that same section of $G(C)$. Under Steps 3 and 4 all nonzero summands and their sections are identified by identity maps. Step 2 preserves their sheafification-unit images. Thus the unit and counit diagrams commute on every presheaf summand, hence after sheafification by its universal property.

source.place: Tag 03DI, proof of lemma-extension-by-zero; explicit unit/counit formulas

proof.text: For nested subterminals $A\hookrightarrow B\hookrightarrow1$, write $h^*$ for restriction from the $B$-slice to the $A$-slice and $h_!$ for its left adjoint. Composition of the natural Hom bijections of Step 1 identifies $j_{B!}h_!$ with $j_{A!}$: both represent $F\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F,j_A^*G)$, and the identification is uniquely fixed by the summand section maps. The nested-open map $j_{A!}h^*H\to j_{B!}H$ is $j_{B!}$ of the counit $h_!h^*H\to H$. By Step 5 it sends the summand indexed by $C\to A$ to the summand indexed by its composite $C\to B$, carrying $s$ to $s$. Restriction and the intersection identifications send the same section to $s$ whenever that summand exists; otherwise the source is zero. Therefore their diagrams with nested-open maps commute, again by the sheafification universal property. This covers the inclusions of $W$ in $U,V$ and their inclusions in $1$.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 04IY (lemma-relocalize); composition of the displayed adjunctions on generators

proof.text: For any $C$, pullback stability of the covering sieve generated by $U,V\to1$ says that $C\times U\to C$ and $C\times V\to C$ generate a covering sieve. If $j_U^*M=j_V^*M=0$, a section $s\in M(C)$ restricts to zero on both objects, since they map to $U$ and $V$. Every arrow in the covering sieve factors through one of them, so all restrictions of $s$ on that sieve are zero. Uniqueness in the sheaf condition gives $s=0$. Thus all section modules vanish and $M=0$. The same argument applied to the section $t_C(s)$ proves that a morphism $t:M\to N$ whose two restrictions are zero is zero. This uses only the site axioms and the sheaf condition in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], not existence of points.

source.place: Agent cover/separatedness argument for the two covering subterminals

proof.text: For module maps $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ whose restrictions are exact, the restrictions of $gf$ vanish, so Step 7 gives $gf=0$. Form $H=\ker(g)/\operatorname{im}(f)$ in the abelian category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By exactness of the two restriction functors from Step 1 and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], $j_Z^*H\cong\ker(j_Z^*g)/\operatorname{im}(j_Z^*f)=0$ for $Z=U,V$. Step 7 gives $H=0$, which is exactly exactness at $B$. Conversely, the two exact functors preserve exactness by the same cited lemma. Applying this to each successive triple proves joint detection for sequences, including endpoint mono/epi conditions by inserting zero objects.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor); agent application to the cover

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to exact restriction: $H^q(j_Z^*K)\cong j_Z^*H^q(K)$ naturally, for every integer $q$. Step 7 now gives joint detection of vanishing of each $H^q(K)$. For a chain map $a$, exact restriction preserves its cohomology kernels and cokernels by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. If both restrictions of $a$ are quasi-isomorphisms, these kernels and cokernels restrict to zero; Step 7 makes them zero, so each $H^q(a)$ is an isomorphism and $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The converse follows from the cohomology comparison. Finally apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to all exact restriction and extension functors of Step 1: their termwise actions descend to the ordinary unbounded derived categories as triangulated functors. The natural cohomology comparison descends through localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so the same cohomological vanishing tests hold there, with no boundedness assumption.

One commit. The item's statement, stmt_deps and blueprint fields are byte-identical to live, there are no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and no SGA is cited. I read every cited statement. lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact gives exact j^* and j_! and the Hom bijection for any object and comm ring sheaf. The special-case clause of def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf (at most one map to U) applies because Z and W are subterminal. lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-restriction needs continuous and cocontinuous functors between small sites; step 2 checks this for the slice forgetful functor, and it gives the unit-normalized comparison. The exact-functor H^q, homology and triangulated results are mathlib leaves. Step by step: (3) the restricted P_F equals F (module version of 0F6Z). (4) An arrow C→V is the same as the unique arrow C→W=U×V over U, so the presheaves agree before sheafification; the k_V^* value comes from relocalization. (5) The unit and counit are determined on summand generators; I checked j_U^*ε_V against the k_U counit. (6) Nested maps use uniqueness of left adjoints and relocalization. (7) The pulled-back cover {C×U,C×V} plus sheaf separation proves zero and zero-morphism detection, with no points used. (8) Homology detection. (9) H^q commutes with restriction, giving quasi-isomorphism detection and unbounded triangulated functors. Edge cases tested: U=V=1, U=1, disjoint U and V, objects locally but not globally over V (sheafification is taken before identification), zero ring.
